## What managing South Loop takes.

### Dearborn Park and Central Station
The planned communities south of the Loop mix townhome courts, mid-rises, and private drives with layered association structures. We manage within master-and-sub-association frameworks without losing any community's interests in the shuffle.

### Amenity-tower operations
Newer South Loop high-rises run on garage podiums, pool decks, and club floors. We size the service contracts and reserves these amenity packages actually require, so assessments stay honest.

### Event-season logistics
With Grant Park festivals and marathon weekend at the doorstep, we plan traffic, parking, and building-access logistics ahead of the city's biggest weekends instead of reacting to them.

## South Loop boards ask us first.

### Do you manage townhome communities in Dearborn Park and Central Station?
Yes. We manage South Loop townhome and homeowner associations, including communities with private streets and shared drives, coordinating snow removal, landscaping, and capital work, and navigating master-association relationships where they exist.

### Can CenterPoint handle a high-rise with a large amenity package?
Yes. Amenity-rich buildings are a South Loop signature, and we manage them daily: pool and fitness contracts, engineer staffing, package-room logistics, and reserve planning for the systems behind the amenities.

### Does CenterPoint manage associations in South Loop?
Yes. CenterPoint Association Management provides condominium, HOA, and townhome association management in South Loop, Chicago (ZIP 60605, 60616). Every association gets a dedicated manager, monthly financial reporting, and board support grounded in Illinois association law.

### How much does association management cost in South Loop?
Management starts at $20 per unit per month, quoted as a flat monthly fee based on your association's size, building systems, financial complexity, and service scope. It is never a percentage of your budget. See [pricing](https://www.centerpointmgmt.com/pricing) for what drives the fee.

### How does a South Loop association switch to CenterPoint?
Plan on a managed 30 to 60 day transition after your board gives notice under its current contract. We retrieve records from the outgoing manager, set up banking and vendor relationships, notify owners, and open board and resident access. Call [773.728.0652](tel:+17737280652) or [request a proposal](https://www.centerpointmgmt.com/contact).

### How should a South Loop board compare management companies?
Compare at least three firms on the same terms: an active Illinois community association management firm license, a licensed manager, a flat monthly fee in writing, after-hours emergency coverage, and a written transition plan. Our free [proposal scorecard](https://www.centerpointmgmt.com/tools/compare-management-proposals) helps boards score proposals side by side.
